drivingQuestion: How is the get valid if the husband never passed from her presence?
outcomeNote: Rav Huna's gloss answers; R' Yoḥanan's alternative follows in the next unit

segments.he: ״הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁאֶעֱבוֹר״ וְכוּ׳: וְהָא לָא עֲבַר! אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מַאי ״פָּנַיִךְ״ – תַּשְׁמִישׁ; וְאַמַּאי קָרֵי לֵיהּ ״פָּנַיִךְ״ – לִישָּׁנָא מְעַלְּיָא נָקֵט.
segments.en: § The continuation of the mishna states: If a husband said to his wife: «This is your bill of divorce» if at «any time I will depart» from your presence for thirty consecutive days, then even if he was continually going and coming, going and coming, since he was not secluded with her during these thirty days this is a valid bill of divorce. The Gemara challenges: «But did he not pass» from her presence during this time, as he was going and coming the entire time? «Rav Huna said: What» is the meaning of the term «your presence» in this context? It means «sexual intercourse.» His actual condition was that if he will not engage in sexual intercourse with her for thirty days then the bill of divorce will be valid. «And why does he call» sexual intercourse «your presence? He employed a euphemistic expression» when he made his condition.
